kind: independent final frozen managed group SDK and returned-error fix review
readonly_contract: No SQL/schema/accounting/session or database/WAL mutation; existing SQLite SHM read-lock/read-mark bookkeeping permitted. No new sidecars or immutable-mode stale reads. This helper reports current membership only and does not register/adopt/contain or authorize termination.
source_review: POSIX only. Requires original absolute non-link ledger path and existing regular DB/WAL/SHM files before opening; missing sidecars reject before sqlite.connect. Uses URI mode=ro, never Accounting or immutable=1. SQL authorizer permits only SELECT/READ/transaction actions.

Checks original project/version, running producer session, original pending reservation/run/unit/output bindings, live native guardian/coordinator and unchanged output directory identity. Shared read validation rejects mismatched reservation/output/policy/helper identities.

Target must already belong to caller group/session. Requires exactly one recorded live native gate identity for that group, group=session=anchor PID, and matching caller/target/anchor current native kernel membership. Checks native birth identities/membership twice.

Releases first read transaction and reads current active bindings again, comparing original run/unit/reservation/output/owner identities and the exact unique gate. This prevents relying only on the first stale running snapshot.

No SQL mutation, producer registration/adoption, signals, process launch, resource cleanup or accounting declaration occurs inside managed_group_identity. All opened read connections close in finally on success or rejection.

Tests source verifies real POSIX gate membership/default or explicit target, foreign/unregistered target rejection, inactive/malformed/reused/dead owners, unsupported Windows behavior, and missing-sidecar pre-open failure. Trace/total_changes and DB/WAL hash comparisons permit only existing SHM bookkeeping.

limitations: Pure SDK probes replace filesystem/OS/native identity/SQLite operations entirely with in-memory doubles and execute only the actual SDK function. They test guards and read-only call intent; they do not establish actual kernel identity or SQLite file behavior.

Source uses a pre-open existence/type check for active native sidecars, not an atomic filesystem sandbox against hostile concurrent replacement. Ordinary process/group exit races after return remain explicit in the SDK contract.
Real group and cleanup tests, actual SQLite read locks/bytes, Windows fixture execution and full CI remain root-owned; this report does not relabel source review or pure probes as those executions.
